Issued at 203 AM CDT Wed Oct 14 2026

A Freeze Warning and Frost Advisory remain in place early this 
morning, and are set to run through 14Z. As of ~06Z, sites over 
central and portions of north central South Dakota are evolving as 
expected, and there are some sites reporting temperatures near 
freezing already. The main questions for these headlines now are 
Brown, Spink, McPherson, and Edmunds Counties. A stratus deck has 
been in place over Brown County this morning, and showing no signs 
of moving out, meaning that the area will have great difficulty 
reaching 32 degrees this morning. The other three aforementioned 
counties have been able to cool off a bit more, but this same 
stratus deck is moving overhead, and may cut off the ability to cool 
further in that area too. As of the time of issuance of this 
discussion the Warnings will remain in place, but a possible early 
cancellation will be on the table for those counties depending on 
how trends evolve this morning. 

A closed upper-level low will move up into the region late today and 
bring the next chances for rain. A last-minute northward shift in 
the track has increased expected rainfall totals, particularly over 
central South Dakota. Expectations in that area are now for a tenth 
to a quarter of an inch, with perhaps some localized values greater 
than a quarter of an inch along and south of I-90. Rainfall values 
will drop off moving north, meaning that the rest of South Dakota 
and western Minnesota will still likely see only a few hundredths at 
best. 

A cold front will move across the region early Thursday, behind 
which winds will turn northwesterly and increase as the pressure 
gradient tightens. Latest NBM probabilities for gusts reaching Wind 
Advisory criteria (45 miles per hour or greater) reach up to 60-80% 
over central and north central South Dakota. Under a cold air 
advection regime, NBM biases are to under forecast wind speeds, 
which only increases confidence for the potential for a Wind 
Advisory on Thursday. Dew points drop about 10-15 degrees behind the 
front, ushering in drier air during the afternoon. With the strong 
wind and dry air combination in place, Grassland Fire Danger will be 
pushed up to High to Very High over central and north central South 
Dakota. Humidity values will still remain at 35-45 percent in that 
area even with the drier airmass, so a Red Flag Warning does not 
appear to be on the table Thursday. 

Slightly warmer temperatures are expected overnight tonight and into 
Thursday morning due to cloud cover limiting radiational cooling. 
Parts of northeastern South Dakota and western Minnesota may dip 
down to 36 degrees and facilitate frost development, but confidence 
in that scenario is somewhat low. Friday morning will see much 
clearer skies along with some lingering weak cold air advection 
lingering overnight, both of which will facilitate the return of sub-
freezing temperatures over much of the region (with the best chances 
being over north central and parts of northeastern South Dakota). 
Areas that do not reach freezing will likely be cold enough to see 
frost, although there is still some question as to whether or not 
humidity will fully recover Friday morning. 

Over the weekend and into next week, signal is strong for an upper-
level ridge to move overhead. 850mb temperatures of 15-20 degrees 
Celsius will be in place over the weekend as a result, which is 
above the 90th percentile for this time of year. Expect those above 
normal temperatures to translate to the surface, at least into the 
upper 60s to 70s across the forecast area. In terms of 
precipitation, dry conditions are expected while the ridge remains 
over the region.
